subject: AI & Agents
title: What Makes Something Intelligent?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Makes Something Intelligent?.

hook.text: A calculator solves equations faster than any human. Is it intelligent?

buildup.text: Alan Turing proposed a test in 1950: if a machine fools a human into thinking it's human, call it intelligent.

discovery.text: Intelligence isn't one thing. It spans reasoning, adapting, learning, and creating.

twist.text: Modern AI aces some of those skills and completely fails at others.

climax.text: A language model writes essays but can't count the letters in 'strawberry.'

punchline.text: Intelligence is a spectrum, not a switch.

quiz.question: Who proposed the famous test for machine intelligence in 1950?

details.summary: Intelligence is hard to define even in humans. Commonly cited elements include learning, reasoning, adapting, and problem-solving. AI exhibits some of these in narrow domains but lacks holistic intelligence.
details.whyItMatters: Without a clear definition of intelligence, it is impossible to know when AI has achieved it. This ambiguity fuels both premature claims of AI sentience and unrealistic dismissals of AI capability.
takeaways: There is no universally agreed definition of intelligence
AI demonstrates narrow aspects like pattern recognition
Holistic intelligence including consciousness remains uniquely human

faq.question: Is AI actually intelligent?
faq.answer: AI is intelligent in the narrow sense of excelling at specific tasks. But it lacks self-awareness, general reasoning, and the ability to understand meaning — qualities most people include in their definition of intelligence.

faq.question: Will we ever all agree on what intelligence means?
faq.answer: Probably not. Intelligence is a rich, multifaceted concept that philosophers, psychologists, and neuroscientists define differently. This ambiguity will continue to complicate discussions about whether AI is truly intelligent.
